This tick owed the build "make - populate the absent set". Pricing it
showed the wheel declares no subtracted row, so the change was
contained. Then reading diff_row showed there was nothing to change: it
already does ef_make(name_set_diff(pa, pb), name_set_union(aa, pb), ta),
removing the name from the present set and adding it to the absent set,
exactly as SYNTAX's E - F = E & !F says.

So the previous entry's mechanism is retracted. "The artifact subtracts
it instead, E - F = E" came from reading an error message's display as
though it were the row. A display is not a measurement, and that is the
second time this arc has billed me for the difference.

The leak is real and sharper than the framing, and needs no subtraction:
fn run(f) with A + !B = f() accepts run(() => opb()), and the medium
volunteers the reason — T_OverDeclared, function run declares A + !B but
body only uses Pure. The callback's row never reaches the enclosing fn's
row when that fn carries its own declared row, so the !B has nothing to
check.

Why the battery misses it is one clause: leak-hof-annotated refuses the
same shape because fn run(f: () -> Int) = f() has no with-clause, so
run's row is inferred, carries f's row, and the caller's !E catches it.
Phase 1 closed the unannotated form via the signature keep-set; the
annotated form was not closed with it, and every existing HOF crucible
puts the negation on the caller rather than on the function that takes
the callback.

Banked as annotated-hof-loses-its-param-row with the six-line repro. The
crucible stays held back until the fix.

mentl/82a7e42:
The layer-3 analysis substrate goes from dormant scaffold to real.
infer_fn brackets every fn body in region_enter/region_exit: body
allocations tag with the fn's own region, nested decls nest their own.
check_escape reads three verdicts at the return boundary: a value tagged
with the fn's OWN region re-tags into the PARENT region — the return is
a TRANSFER (Hbeta.own.region-return-transfer, the
result-region-as-parameter form): the caller owns the value now, which
is exactly what makes the region drop safe as the future arena reset.
An outer or global tag already outlives the return; a dead tag is the
genuine escape, reported with both spans.

Region ids start at 1 — 0 stays the no-region/global sentinel every tag
test reads, so the first live region can never collide with it. The
dormancy had hidden a wrong-end stack (the sect-9 class: region_enter
pushed at the FRONT while current_region/region_exit read last/drop_last
— an enter/pop queue that never had two elements to expose it); pushes
now go at the END like every Mentl stack.

Soundness traced before the byte: tags key AST construction nodes and
cross-fn value flow rides untagged CALL nodes, so a transferred
composite's stale inner field-tags can never re-check falsely. The
class-aware tag lookup (a block body unifies with its tail; the raw
handle misses the class-mate) is the arena increment's named burden, as
is mutation-site checking — which needs result/argument region
POLYMORPHISM first, or the wheel's ref-buffer idiom false-floods
(Tofte-Talpin's actual lesson).

Measured: the wheel self-compiles under LIVE regions with ZERO escapes —
the Hylo-quiet bar on ~37k lines (every legal return transfers, no false
flags). mn-region-transfer=5 enters the baseline (71 micros). March

Verified on wasmtime 43: a single cont.new+resume under the WASI
command entry _start panics ptr::eq(head, self) (the same internal
assertion double-resume trips) even with a memory export; --invoke
works, _start does not, and no -W/-O/-C flag avoids it. wasmtime runs
the command on its own fiber and a user continuation violates its
continuation-stack invariant. Every real Mentl program runs via
_start, so native typed continuations cannot ship as the multi-shot
substrate on wasmtime 43 — they are the O(1) future, an !Outside
dependency until upstream carries them under _start.

The shipping path is the pure-Mentl re-execution driver (all ordinary
handlers, works under _start): resume(v) re-runs the body thunk under a
one-shot replay handler. Its direct form is proven (reexec-model.mn ->
30) and correct for unconditionally-performed ops (mn-multishot). The
general case needs the arm-internal-perform gap closed (named peer
Hbeta.lower.arm-internal-perform-scope) so a re-run's perform resolves
to the inner replay instead of re-entering the outer handler — core
handler correctness, !Outside-clean. Findings banked in
tests/native-cont/README.md and band B.
mentl/82467f2:
The last gap before first-light. A handler is (a ! E+r) ⟿ (a ! R+r): it removes
the handled effect E AND adds its arms' residual row R. Mentl carries E (the
Handler<E> type) but drops R — so `~>` can't transform the row, and every
map/for_each loses the effects performed in its arms (the L1 lower-trap root,
masked by the perform-dispatch's silent slot-0 fallback; see
protocol_handler_effect_typing + protocol_fallback_masked_effect_row_gap).

Phase 1 lays the foundation: SchemeKind gains HandlerKind(handled_ename: String,
residual_row_handle: Int) as tag 6 (APPENDED — seed tag-constant stability). The
residual row is a LIVE row var (union-find), config-polymorphic; `~>` will read
it as `(row(expr) − E) ⊕ R`. cache.mn Pack/Unpack round-trips tag 6 (raw handle
— the resolved-row form for cross-compile handler caching is peer
Hβ.cache.handler-residual-row, post-L1; the single-file first-light path never
round-trips it). Nothing constructs HandlerKind yet — clean foundation; census
holds 171, micros green. Phases 2-6 (register_handler computes R; handler
let-polymorphism; `~>` applies the transform; seed mirror; retire the fallback)
follow per the blueprint.

CallExpr(VarRef("list_index"), [xs, i]). Parser produces
IndexExpr(receiver, index) as a semantic AST node; infer
dispatches on receiver's chase-deep Ty (TList → list_index runtime
call; TTuple → compile-time slot via LFieldLoad; TRecord by int-
key → record_get); lower projects at its cursor.

Substrate cursors:

- parser.mn: TLBracket arm produces IndexExpr instead of CallExpr fold
- infer.mn: NExpr(IndexExpr(receiver, index)) arm — index binds to

  at the lower cursor (peer Hβ.lower.indexexpr-tuple-slot collapses
  to LFieldLoad when receiver Ty is TTuple with constant index)

Per the eight interrogations:
- Graph: IndexExpr is one handle; receiver + index are children
- Handler: parser produces; infer/lower project; no handler
- Verb: |> postfix application (postfix_loop continuation)
- Row: +Memory at runtime (list_index reads); +Alloc only for new

  ultimate) elides runtime bounds check
- Gradient: type-known receiver → compile-time slot OR runtime call
- Reason: Located span + Inferred("subscript ...") per cursor read

commits to list_index dispatch before infer knows receiver type).

mentl/8226380:
Three structural fixes that unblock Phase H:

1. Forward sibling closure patching (wasm_construct.lux, wasm_emit.lux):
   Mutually recursive inner functions (a calls b, b defined after a) had
   corrupted captures — the forward reference stored garbage instead of
   the sibling's closure pointer. The emitter now patches forward
   references after each closure is created, generalizing the existing
   self-reference patch. Also pre-scans FnStmt names in lower_closure.lux
   so forward references don't propagate as free vars to enclosing scope.
   wasm_check.lux (full compiler in WASM) now runs on wasmtime.

2. Effect cancellation (infer.lux):
   perform(E) + handle(E) = Pure. When a handle block absorbs all named
   effects, close the open row to EfPure. has_tvars purity proof verified.

3. NoneExpr deleted (parser.lux, infer.lux, lower.lux, codegen.lux, own.lux,
   pipeline.lux): Parse failure is an effect, not a value. The ParseError
   handler no longer resumes with a sentinel — it returns [] and stops.
   NoneExpr removed from the Expr ADT and all downstream consumers.

Also: slice→index conversion across check.lux/eff.lux/ty.lux/pipeline.lux
(O(n²)→O(n)), duplicate join deleted from eff.lux, HONK fallbacks cleaned up,
max call arity tracked in supercollector, debug output removed from main.rs.

ARCHITECTURE.md: replaced the "nothing can surpass this" formal argument
with an explicit set of five falsifiable bets and what would break each,
fixed the 1.58-bits/weight → 16× capacity conflation (it's a storage and
bandwidth win, not a capability multiplier), documented the current

distill.rs: the previous MDL accounting mixed units (pattern in raw bits,
episodes missing the 32× f32 factor, residuals using log2(1+variance)
with no noise model). Replaced it with a proper two-part code: pattern
overhead + raw baseline minus Gaussian likelihood-ratio savings against
the batch variance, summed per dimension and floored at zero so a
cluster can never be scored as worse than the null. Added a coherence
gate — reject clusters whose actual_token distribution has entropy
above 2 bits, because otherwise the embedding-aligned correction
direction averages to noise. Thresholds moved into a DistillConfig.

and reject-too-small.
